title: Five years with Hampton, Johnny Griffin and Hampton's love of tenor players
summary: Cobb dates his Hampton years 1942 to 1947, says Johnny Griffin joined in 1945, and explains Hampton converts alto players to tenor because of Herschel Evans.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: : Well, what were the years you were with Hamp? What --
: '42 to '47? Well, I mean that was a very substantial band at that time, wasn't it?
Some of the best years of my life.
: Yeah. Yeah, I remember seeing you in '46, I think it was. And that would be -- I think that was Johnny Griffin.
Johnny Griffin (inaudible). He came in in '45.

We were at the Regal Theater in Chicago, and Lionel went over to (inaudible) a show for the kids at Dusevel High School and heard Johnny Play on an album. And that's when he got Johnny. (Inaudible) always good for taking you off alto and put you on tenor. He put Illinois Jacquet on tenor, who was an alto player, put Johnny Griffin on tenor, who was an alto player.
And Hamp's a tenor freak because of Herschel Evans. He used to work --
: That's who was with his band on the coast.
He used to work with Herschel on the West Coast before Basie, and he said he used to work -- to work

to tune Herschel up. He said, (inaudible), Herschel even tune up with soul. He said, I hit the A for him on the piano. I beat him to work so I could hit the A for him. He said, I'd say, blow on (Inaudible) I just say, ha-aco-o-o-o, with soul, ha-ao-o-o. And that gas Hamp. And Hamp loves tenor players today. And that's why he loved Illinois. He loved me, He loved Johnny Griffin and ones he converted. I was already on tenor.

But he converted alto players into tenor players because he loved tenor because of Herschel. He loved Herschel. And Hamp was a soul man himself, but he said Herschel had more soul than anybody I know. And he did.
Yeah, of course, (inaudible) we don't have that much by Herschel because, you know, Lester took more solos than Herschel in Basie's band.
It's sentimental for you, though, isn't it?
